profile.reading: This OpenStreetMap record, tagged telecom=data_center and named simply "Verizon," is located near Sahara Avenue in central Las Vegas, Nevada, in Clark County. It is confirmed to be a genuinely separate location from a similarly named "Verizon North Las Vegas" record roughly 8.5 miles away elsewhere in the county, rather than a duplicate map entry for the same building. Verizon Communications is a real, major, publicly traded US telecommunications company headquartered in New York City, but its legacy wireline network only serves as the incumbent local carrier in nine eastern states, and Nevada is not among them, making a traditional telephone central office an unlikely explanation here. A Verizon Wireless mobile network facility, such as a switching center serving the Las Vegas metro area, is a more plausible category given Verizon Wireless's nationwide cellular footprint, though this is inference rather than a confirmed fact. This OSM record carries even less identifying detail than its North Las Vegas counterpart, lacking even an operator tag beyond the bare name. No address, capacity information, or independent news coverage could be located this session because search-tool quota was exhausted. This entry is filed as an honest, unresolved case, most plausibly Verizon network infrastructure rather than a commercial colocation data center, without asserting fabricated building specifications.

sources.title: Equinix Completes Acquisition of 29 Data Centers from Verizon

profile.research_note: Verizon sold its commercial colocation/data-center business (29 facilities) to Equinix in 2017 and exited the public colocation market; it does not publish colocation spec sheets. These rows are Verizon-operated network facilities (switching centers, wireless MSC/central-office buildings) rather than for-lease colocation space, and no public technical spec page exists for them. Marked specs_unpublished rather than guess.

reading.body:
This record exists as an OpenStreetMap entry tagged as a Verizon facility near Sahara Avenue in central Las Vegas, confirmed as a distinct location from another Verizon site 8.5 miles away in North Las Vegas. No published power capacity, address details, or independent confirmation of its function could be located, and research resources were exhausted before a full identification was possible. The facility is more plausibly Verizon Wireless network infrastructure, such as a mobile switching center serving the Las Vegas metro area, than a commercial colocation data center, but this remains inference rather than established fact.

No specifications were published for this campus, so no assessment of AI hosting capacity is possible. Nevada as a state shows only 10.37 megawatts of published data center capacity across all mapped facilities, ranking this entry third among those published figures, yet that ranking reflects the absence of confirmed data rather than a confirmed power supply.

This facility does not meet the threshold for inclusion in analysis of grid-constrained AI scaling. Without published power capacity, colocation certification, or independent reporting, it cannot be read as material to decisions about where AI infrastructure sits or how the grid shapes compute deployment. The exhaustion of available research sources leaves this entry unresolved.
